scope: The black Sculpted display cover with its crown's pockets, taken off this plate when Derek stopped the print and snapped onto a Sculpted tip from an earlier plate. This plate's own tip was not finished.
tried: the printed cover snapped onto a Sculpted tip from an earlier plate
observations: Photos of the recent fit from the display cover from the print I just stopped on mark2 with that display cover on one of our other faucet tips.

agent_reading.author: Claude, from the photos; not Derek's words.
agent_reading.front: The arch is closed over the cap at its centre. Each shoulder stands open, widest low on the shoulder, and the opening runs on down to the side's fore tip, which stands off the neck.
agent_reading.sides: Along the neck the side's edge lies close from behind the fore tip back. The aft tip stands off the neck by about what the fore tip does.
agent_reading.estimates: Scaled against the dispense face's layer lines, the shoulders stand roughly 0.2 to 0.3 mm off the cap at their widest and each tip roughly 0.3 mm off the neck. That is about the fixed amount this cover's ends were let out by.
agent_reading.limits: Photographs only. No opening was measured on the part. Which earlier tip the cover is on is not stated.

image_processing: Saved as this session received them, JPEGs about two thousand pixels on their long side.

images.view: The front arch from one side and behind the dispense face: light between the arch and the cap from the shoulder up toward the centre, none under the front rim below it.
The cover's side along the neck, from the tube's side: its edge lies along the neck from the fore tip back.
The tip from behind its tube, the cover's side edge on: the edge and its aft tip beside the neck.
One front shoulder, close, from the dispense face: an opening between the cap's rim and the arch, widest low on the shoulder.
The same shoulder from lower, down to the side's fore tip: the opening runs down the shoulder and the fore tip stands off the neck.
The front arch from in front and above: closed over the cap's centre, open down the far shoulder to the fore tip.
The first view closer: light between the arch and the cap at the shoulder.
